articles.title: Energy-Saving System for Marine Generators Touts 10% Fuel Savings
articles.summary: NYK Line, MTI Co., Oshima Shipbuilding, Terasaki Electric and Daihatsu Infinearth have verified the energy-saving performance and operational safety of the Hz Controller System, an energy-saving system for marine generators developed through joint testing.
articles.body: Energy-Saving System for Marine Generators Touts 10% Fuel Savings Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 20, 2026 Copyright Xavier MARCHANT/AdobeStock NYK Line, MTI Co., Oshima Shipbuilding, Terasaki Electric and Daihatsu Infinearth have verified the energy-saving performance and operational safety of the Hz Controller System, an energy-saving system for marine generators developed through joint testing. General sales of the system will now begin. Building on their joint research, the five companies will expand deployment beyond NYK-operated vessels, promoting installation on newbuildings and retrofitting on existing ships owned by other shipowners. The System reduces power consumption and generator fuel consumption by lowering the generator frequency while maintaining the performance required by onboard equipment. This is possible because onboard equipment such as pumps and motors that operate in conjunction with the power supply frequency is designed to deliver the required performance even under anticipated severe conditions and may therefore have excess capacity during normal navigation. Specifically, the System switches between the regular frequency and a lower energy-saving frequency according to shipboard conditions within the range specified by ship classification rules. It utilizes generator frequency control technology (Patent Number JP6238600) that is jointly patented by NYK and Tsuneishi Shipbuilding. Demonstration tests confirmed an approximately 10% reduction in generator fuel consumption compared with operation at the regular frequency. Subsequent verification on an increasing number of vessels equipped with the system confirmed a similar reduction. For general sales, Terasaki Electric will be responsible for the design and supply of the System, while Daihatsu Infinearth will expand its lineup of generator engines compatible with the System.

articles.title: 1 MW floating wave energy converter gets green light for test site deployment
articles.summary: WEDUSEA, a €19.6 million collaborative project bringing together 14 European partners, has secured a marine license that allows the installation...
articles.body: Tidal & Wave Energy November 20, 2026 · 1 minute ago 1 MW floating wave energy converter gets green light for test site deployment NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email EMEC WEDUSEA, a €19.6 million collaborative project bringing together 14 European partners, has secured a marine license that allows the installation of a 1 MW OE Buoy floating wave energy converter and associated moorings at the European Marine Energy Centre's (EMEC) test site in Orkney. Co-funded by the EU Horizon Europe Programme and Innovate UK, WEDUSEA, which brings together 14 partners from industry and academia across Ireland, the UK, France, Germany and Spain, aims to create a step change for the wave energy industry and support its progression towards commercialization. The marine license granted by the Marine Directorate, previously Marine Scotland, allows the 1 MW-rated, unmanned floating oscillating water column device, developed by OceanEnergy, to be deployed at EMEC. Its only moving part, the turbine rotor, sits on deck above the waves, while all electrical equipment is housed below deck in a sealed machine room. As waves cause air trapped within the OE Buoy hull to oscillate, the airflow drives the turbine to generate electricity. This electricity will be exported to the grid via an underwater umbilical and export cable, EMEC explained. The OE Buoy and its mooring system will be installed at Berth 5 at the Billia Croo wave energy test site. Furthermore, EMEC has developed an extensive environmental monitoring plan for the deployment, which will monitor the habitat above and below the water’s surface in the vicinity of the OE Buoy. The monitoring program will begin before installation to establish a baseline of benthic and pelagic activity in the deployment area, helping to build understanding of the marine environment before, during and following deployment. November 20, 2026 (Credit: US Coast Guard) The U.S. Coast Guard has commissioned its newest Sentinel-class fast response cutter, USCGC Marvin Perrett (WPC 1164), during a ceremony in New Orleans, ahead of the vessel's deployment to its homeport in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Coast Guard said the vessel would strengthen its capacity to conduct maritime security, border protection and search and rescue missions in the region. The cutter is named after Marvin Perrett, a New Orleans native and Coast Guard veteran who operated Higgins landing craft during World War II, participating in the Normandy landings and subsequent operations in southern France and the Pacific. articles.body: Cabling November 20, 2026 · 1 minute ago Nexans completes deep-water cable laying ops off Australia for Chevron NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Nexans Nexans has completed the laying and trenching of the high-voltage dynamic cable for Chevron's Jansz-Io Compression (J-IC) project offshore Western Australia. The cable-laying vessel (CLV) Nexans Aurora installed 26 buoyancy modules and trenched 30 kilometers of cable, after which it left Australia on October 23. J-IC uses subsea compression to sustain gas supply to the Gorgon LNG and domestic gas plants on Barrow Island. The 145 kV cable, about 135 kilometers long, runs from the island to a floating field control station, which powers and controls the compressors on the seabed. The completed operation included the overboarding and pull-in of the cable head to the field control station, installation of the buoyancy modules using a horizontal method developed, laying of the cable in its dynamic configuration, installation of about 200 meters of vortex-induced vibration (VIV) strakes in the Scarp section, cable lay up the Scarp, float-out and pull-in of the second cable end at Barrow Island, as-laid survey and cable trenching. Before handover, the remaining work includes cable jointing at the field control station and on Barrow Island, rock stabilization along the last 28 kilometers of the route, and final soak test, planned for February. Nexans Chevron sanctioned the Jansz-Io compression project in early July 2021 and ordered the field control station from the Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering (DSME) shipyard, now known as Hanwha Ocean, a few months later. articles.body: Europe Offshore Renewables Scotland greenlights 1 GW floating offshore wind project Bojan Lepic November 20, 2026 0 646 1 minute read Ingka Group Ingka Group The Scottish Government has granted offshore planning consent for the 1GW Muir Mhòr floating wind farm being developed by Fred. Olsen Seawind off the Aberdeenshire coast. Located approximately 63 km east of Peterhead, the project will comprise up to 67 floating wind turbines capable of generating enough electricity to meet the equivalent annual consumption of around 1.2m homes. The offshore approval follows onshore planning permission granted last year for the project’s underground cables and substation infrastructure. Muir Mhòr was awarded seabed rights in Scotland’s ScotWind leasing round in 2022 and is among the country’s most advanced commercial-scale floating wind developments. Fred. Olsen Seawind took full ownership of the project earlier this year after acquiring Vattenfall’s 50% interest. The developer is targeting the start of electricity generation in the early 2030s, subject to further commercial and investment decisions. The project has already awarded £18.4m in development contracts, including £7.96m to Scottish suppliers. The latest approval comes with conditions requiring measures to address the wind farm’s potential impact on commercial fisheries and seabirds. The Scottish Fishermen’s Federation criticised the decision, arguing that questions remain about whether fishing vessels can operate safely around the project’s floating foundations, moorings, and subsea cables. Scotland currently has more than 11GW of consented offshore wind capacity, according to the government. The consent is a significant development milestone for Muir Mhòr, although the project has yet to reach a final investment decision. articles.body: Exploration & Production November 20, 2026 · 1 minute ago Türkiye's seismic vessel exploring Pakistan's oil & gas potential in its second overseas mission NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Oruç Reis. Source: Turkish Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources Türkiye's national seismic research vessel has embarked on its second overseas operation, having arrived in Pakistan where it will be deployed to assess the country's hydrocarbon potential. A welcome ceremony was held today, November 20, at the Port of Karachi where the vessel Oruç Reis has docked, before starting to collect seismic data in the Indus and Makran basins. Within the scope of the Indus-C Block seismic project, Oruç Reis will carry out 3D seismic data collection activities in a 670 km2 area located approximately 120 kilometers off Karachi Port. This is part of the scope of the agreements signed in 2025 between Turkish Petroleum (TPAO) and Pakistan's energy companies Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL), Mari Energies, and Oil & Gas Development Company (OGDCL). "Our two nations share common values and deep bonds of brotherhood. The strength of the bond between our countries comes from centuries of shared history and the genuine affection our peoples feel for one another," Turkish Energy and Natural Resources Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said. "We have taken this partnership into the field. We have completed the licensing process for five blocks, three offshore and two onshore, and have begun fieldwork. TPAO will use Oruç Reis to acquire 3D seismic data across 670 square kilometers of the Indus C Block. We expect the survey to take 52 days, or about two months." According to Minister Bayraktar, the aim is to start drilling next year at sites that will be identified by the collected data. "Our work onshore and offshore in Pakistan will directly strengthen the security of energy supply in both countries and contribute to the prosperity of our peoples. We have discovered hydrocarbons and brought them into production in our own waters. We want to achieve the same success in Pakistan," Bayraktar said.
